title: Pacing, Not Pausing: What School Leaders Should Say to Parents This Week
author: Marcinek, Andrew
summary: Andrew Marcinek argues that AI lab leaders' recent calls to "pace" rather than halt AI development offer a template for how school leaders should talk with families this fall: acknowledge uncertainty honestly rather than project false confidence. Drawing on Dario Amodei's essay calling for embedded safety evaluators and survey data showing most parents feel uninformed about school AI policy, he argues schools' credibility now depends on candor about what is policy, what is pilot, and what remains unknown. He lays out a concrete three-part communication plan modeled on the labs' own transparency push: sort practices into three honest categories, publish a one-page family brief, and hold real two-way listening sessions before problems surface.
points: Frames AI 'pacing' (slowing capability growth to let understanding catch up) as directly analogous to what school leaders should do with families.
Cites National Parents Union survey data: nearly half of parents say their child's school never explained its AI policy.
Recommends sorting AI practices into 'policy,' 'pilot,' and 'still figuring out' and communicating honestly before backlash occurs.
Warns that pretending AI use is fully under control will cost schools parent trust faster than admitting uncertainty.
quotes: He proposed embedding independent evaluators inside the labs, with desks and badges and the right to publish what they find, and committed his own company to doing it first.
I have written before that schools which pretend to have AI solved will lose parents within a year, and I would now shorten that timeline.

When the National Parents Union polled fifteen hundred public school parents this past February, nearly half said their child's school had never told them anything about its AI policy, and more than half said no one had asked for their input.
Send it before the first angry email, not after. Then put a real listening session on the calendar, with teachers in the room and not just administrators.
Amodei's essay is a plan for the labs to show their work to outsiders. Our version of that plan is simpler and older. Show your work to the parents.
